evidence.positive:
Against the running app (build 1087f571b): staged a 10 y.o. 30 kg demo-demo patient (pmrn or3031-fake-573e6f01-..., case 20455) via the admin API, recorded a prior 12 mg Bupivacaine 0.5% nerve-block bolus through POST /api/admin/bolus/patient/{pmrn}/{caseId}, launched the case as loopuser and selected m-bupivacaine via POST /api/cds/medication-selection/{pmrn}/{caseId}. The w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose WARNING prompt returned routeBasedPromptText.NERVE_BLOCK.displayText = "Max dose is 62 mg. Adjust for: Bupivacaine 0.5% / 12 mg Block / at 14:26 on 10/26/2026
". Then drove the real UI with Playwright (login, /app-launch?...forceLaunch=true, + tab, pick Bupivacaine): the [data-rule-id='w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose'] banner innerText was "Max dose is 62 mg. Adjust for: Bupivacaine 0.5% 12 mg Block at 14:26 on 10/26/2026" (screenshot scratch/ui-banner.png).
evidence.negative: The old phrase never appears: the full selection response JSON after the prior bolus contains '. Adjust for:' and does NOT contain ', adjusted for:' (checked with a substring test on the raw body, saved as scratch/selection-after.json). Also ran the same selection before any bolus was recorded (scratch/selection-before.json): the no-prior-admins branch returned displayText "Max dose is 74 mg" with neither phrase, so the 'Adjust for:' wording is confined to the prior-administrations case as the ticket intends.
evidence.red_check: Compiled the parent commit's (2d22e8f59^) AbstractLocalAnestheticWarningOrInfoRule against the container's own /app/classes and /app/libs (lombok @Slf4j replaced by an explicit slf4j logger, plus one WARN line that logs the built prefix text), backed up the shipped class and its $1 inner class (md5 1e26b97fbb8b9d7224c2c156db789ccd), docker cp'd the pre-fix classes into /app/classes and restarted the container. Re-running the identical selection returned displayText "Max dose is 62 mg, adjusted for: ..." (the pre-fix wording; scratch/selection-red.json) and the app log carried 'OR-3031 red check pre-fix warning text active: Max dose is ${NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_DOSE}, adjusted for:'. Reverted by copying the backup classes back (container md5 re-verified equal to the original 1e26b97f...), restarted, waited for readiness, and re-ran the selection: displayText is again "Max dose is 62 mg. Adjust for: ..." (scratch/selection-restored.json).

red_check_signature: OR-3031 red check pre-fix warning text active: Max dose is ${NERVE_BLOCK_REMAINING_DOSE}, adjusted for:
caveats: The prior administration was recorded with the admin bolus debug endpoint rather than by rejecting an a-local-anesthetic-max-dose-save alert in the UI; the banner text is built by the same rule prompt either way, and the UI render was checked on re-selection.

Only the no-explicit-medication-name branch ('Max dose is ...') was exercised at runtime; the combination-product branch ('Max dose of {component} is ...') received the identical edit and is covered by the updated unit tests in LocalAnestheticWarningEvaluationTest but was not rendered here.

The red check used the pre-fix class with an added log line (the ticket's text is never logged by the shipped code), so the signature comes from that instrumented class, not from stock pre-fix logging.
DosingFormBanner.stories.tsx (Storybook fixture) was updated in the PR but Storybook is not part of the running app and was not rendered.

automation.assessment: LocalAnestheticWarningEvaluationTest already pins the exact '. Adjust for:' HTML for both branches at the unit level (8 assertions updated in the PR). qa-suite LAMD-001 exercises the save and scan alerts but never asserts the w-last-local-anesthetic-max-dose banner text. A cheap browser-free supplemental test can lock the user-facing wording in via the medication-selection API, which is where a regression would actually surface.

jira_comment:
Verdict: deploy-ready.

Positive: With a prior 12 mg Bupivacaine block recorded, re-selecting Bupivacaine returned the banner "Max dose is 62 mg. Adjust for:" followed by the administration table, both in the API response and rendered in the dosing form.
Negative: The old ", adjusted for:" wording is absent from the response, and with no prior dose the banner reads "Max dose is 74 mg" with neither phrase.
Red check: Swapping the pre-fix rule class into the running container brought back "Max dose is 62 mg, adjusted for:", and restoring the shipped class brought the new wording back.

Automation: Unit tests already pin the HTML; a supplemental qa-suite API test asserting the banner wording after a prior block is proposed.
